pixavector.subject: vector artwork
pixavector.start: Start with a simple shape or a copy of an existing vector document.
pixavector.work: Use selection to choose an object, then adjust its position, shape, fill and stroke. Keep separate objects for elements you may want to change later.
pixavector.organize: Use layers and groups to keep related artwork together. Check object order when one shape hides another.
pixavector.finish: Keep an editable project copy. Export a separate copy in the format needed by the person or service receiving your artwork.

pixafilm.subject: a video edit
pixafilm.start: Import a few short clips and place them in a sequence. Work with copies of important footage.
pixafilm.work: Arrange clips on the timeline, trim their beginnings and ends, and preview the cuts. Listen to the audio as well as watching the image.
pixafilm.organize: Keep original media available at its original path. Use clearly named tracks and sequences so the project remains understandable.
pixafilm.finish: Save the project separately from the rendered video. Preview the exported result from beginning to end before sharing it.

pixalight.subject: a photo library
pixalight.start: Import a small set of photos into the library before bringing in a large collection. Keep a backup of original files.
pixalight.work: Choose a photo and make a small exposure or color adjustment. Compare the result with the original before making stronger changes.
pixalight.organize: Use the library's organizational controls to narrow down the photos you want to edit. Back up both the catalog and the original files.
pixalight.finish: Export a separate image for sharing. Keep the catalog and originals so you can revise the edit later.

pixapdf.subject: a PDF document
pixapdf.start: Open a copy of a PDF you can safely experiment with. Check the page count and orientation.
pixapdf.work: Choose the task you need, such as reading, commenting or organizing pages. Confirm the target page or selection before applying a change.
pixapdf.organize: Keep an original copy before rearranging or removing pages. Review pages at a readable zoom after editing.
pixapdf.finish: Save to a new file while learning. Reopen the result and check page order, visible content and any security settings you changed.

pixadesign.subject: a page layout
pixadesign.start: Create a document with the page dimensions you need. Begin with one page before building a large publication.
pixadesign.work: Place text and images into the layout. Adjust alignment, spacing and text flow so the page reads clearly.
pixadesign.organize: Use consistent styles and keep linked images accessible. Review every page for missing images or overflowing text.
pixadesign.finish: Save the editable layout. Export a separate PDF when needed, then inspect its pages before sending it to print or publication.

pixainterface.subject: an interface design
pixainterface.start: Create a small design with one screen or frame. Decide what the person using that screen should notice first.
pixainterface.work: Add shapes, text and interface elements, then adjust alignment and spacing. Use a consistent visual hierarchy.
pixainterface.organize: Name screens and layers clearly. Keep related elements together and reuse consistent styling where the editor supports it.
pixainterface.finish: Save the editable design and preview the screens you plan to share. Check exported assets at their intended display size.

pixatexture.subject: a painted 3D texture
pixatexture.start: Begin with a test model or project. Keep an untouched copy of the model and its original textures.
pixatexture.work: Choose a paint target and make a small brush stroke. Check the result on the model before painting a large area.
pixatexture.organize: Keep texture layers and channels organized. Check that you are painting the intended texture set.
pixatexture.finish: Save the editable project before exporting textures. Inspect the exported maps in the program where you intend to use them.

pixamaterial.subject: a procedural material
pixamaterial.start: Start with a small material graph and inspect its preview. Build up complexity gradually.
pixamaterial.work: Connect a small number of nodes, adjust a parameter and watch how the result changes. Change one thing at a time while learning.
pixamaterial.organize: Keep the graph readable and identify the final outputs. Avoid unnecessary complexity until the basic material works.
pixamaterial.finish: Save the editable graph or package. Export the outputs you need and check them in the destination application.

pixaword.subject: a written document
pixaword.start: Create a short document or open a copy of an existing one. Type a few paragraphs before applying extensive formatting.
pixaword.work: Select text to change its formatting. Use paragraph and document controls for spacing and page layout rather than repeated spaces or blank lines.
pixaword.organize: Use consistent headings and styles. Review page breaks, lists and tables as the document grows.
pixaword.finish: Save an editable document. If exporting a PDF or another format, reopen it and check pagination and text layout.

pixasound.subject: an audio session
pixasound.start: Begin with a short audio file or a test recording. Keep playback volume comfortable before experimenting.
pixasound.work: Place audio on tracks, adjust timing and listen to the result. Make small level changes and avoid unwanted clipping.
pixasound.organize: Name tracks clearly and keep source audio available. Save a session copy before major edits.
pixasound.finish: Save the editable session, then export the mix separately. Listen to the entire exported file before sharing it.

pixadeck.subject: a presentation
pixadeck.start: Create a short presentation with a title slide and one content slide.
pixadeck.work: Add text and images with a clear reading order. Keep each slide focused on one main point.
pixadeck.organize: Review slide order and maintain consistent typography and spacing. Check any media you add on the machine that will present it.
pixadeck.finish: Save the editable presentation and test its presentation view. Review any exported PDF or images before distributing them.

pixacad.subject: a CAD drawing
pixacad.start: Start with a simple drawing and confirm the units you intend to use. Keep an original copy of imported drawings.
pixacad.work: Create a few basic entities and inspect their dimensions and positions. Use the editor's precision controls rather than relying only on appearance.
pixacad.organize: Use layers and clear names to separate parts of the drawing. Check coordinates, scale and units before adding detail.
pixacad.finish: Save the editable drawing. Check the chosen format, units and scale when exporting or sharing it with another CAD application.

pixagrid.subject: a spreadsheet
pixagrid.start: Create a small workbook with clear column headings and a few rows of data.
pixagrid.work: Enter values and a simple formula. Check that the result is correct before copying the formula to other cells.
pixagrid.organize: Keep labels, data and calculated results easy to distinguish. Review cell references after moving or copying formulas.
pixagrid.finish: Save the workbook and inspect any exported file. Confirm formulas and totals before relying on the spreadsheet for decisions.

pixaanything.subject: a software exploration
pixaanything.start: Choose software or files you own or are authorized to inspect. Begin with a small, clearly defined question.
pixaanything.work: Use the application's available exploration tools and read the evidence they return. Distinguish confirmed findings from guesses or missing information.
pixaanything.organize: Keep the project focused and review any action that would execute code, change files or affect another device before approving it.
pixaanything.finish: Save the project and its findings. Test any new software you build in an isolated environment before using it with important data.
